answer:
Calculate the pressure drop (delta P) in a horizontal pipe using the Darcy-Weisbach equation.
The pipe is 100 m long with an internal diameter of 50 mm.
The fluid is water at 20°C with density 998 kg/m³ and dynamic viscosity 0.001 Pa·s.
The volumetric flow rate is 2 L/s.
The pipe material is galvanized iron with an internal absolute roughness of 0.15 mm.
First compute the mean flow velocity from the flow rate and pipe cross-sectional area.
Then compute the Reynolds number to determine the flow regime.
Then compute the relative roughness (epsilon divided by diameter).
Determine the Darcy friction factor using the Colebrook-White equation (or an explicit approximation such as Swamee-Jain) given the Reynolds number and relative roughness.
Finally apply the Darcy-Weisbach equation: delta P equals f times (L/D) times (rho times V squared / 2).
Present the final pressure drop in Pascals and also in a more readable unit such as kPa or bar.
Show all intermediate values (velocity, Reynolds number, relative roughness, friction factor) so the result can be verified step by step.
